outcomeNote: a single restriction of the mishna

segments.he: וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁהָה כְּדֵי הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה. אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה כְּלַפֵּי פְנִים, אֲבָל הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה כְּלַפֵּי חוּץ – שָׁהָה אִין, לֹא שָׁהָה לָא.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If «he bowed down, or he tarried» in the Temple courtyard «long enough to bow down,» or he went out by way of a longer route when he could have taken a shorter route, he is liable to bring a sliding-scale offering. «Rava says: They taught» this «only when he bowed down» in the Temple courtyard «facing inward,» toward the Holy of Holies, as that alone is proper bowing. «But» if «he bowed down facing outward,» that is not considered bowing. When he bows facing outward, if «he tarried» in the Temple courtyard long enough to bow down, «yes,» he is liable, but if «he did not tarry» long enough to bow down, he is «not» liable.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא לא שנו אלא שהשתחוה כלפי פנים
moves.summary: Rava restricts the first clause to bowing inward
moves.about: bowing alone creates liability only when facing inward; facing outward requires tarrying
